text: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure. The freezing point drops when solutes such as salt are dissolved in the water.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 kilometres per second. This value is a fundamental constant in modern physics.
Human red blood cells lack a nucleus once mature. Their biconcave shape maximises surface area for oxygen exchange in capillaries.
TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery of a byte stream between two endpoints. UDP, by contrast, offers no delivery guarantees and leaves reliability to the application layer.
Mount Everest straddles the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. Its summit sits at roughly 8,849 metres above sea level.
The English word 'algorithm' derives from the name of the ninth-century Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi. His treatise on Indian numerals shaped medieval European arithmetic.
Bitcoin has a fixed supply cap of twenty-one million coins. New coins enter circulation through block rewards that halve roughly every four years.
DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. Resolvers query a hierarchy of servers beginning at the root zone.
HTTP status codes in the 400 range indicate client errors. Codes in the 500 range indicate server-side problems.
Mitochondria generate most of the ATP in eukaryotic cells through oxidative phosphorylation. They carry their own circular DNA, distinct from the nuclear genome.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans. It covers more surface area than all landmasses combined.
Git stores snapshots of an entire tree, not diffs between files. Objects are addressed by the SHA-1 hash of their content.
The Richter scale is logarithmic. An earthquake of magnitude six releases roughly thirty-two times more energy than one of magnitude five.
ASCII encodes 128 characters using seven bits. UTF-8 extends the scheme to the full Unicode range while remaining backward compatible with ASCII.
Penicillin is produced by moulds of the genus Penicillium. It inhibits the synthesis of peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls.
The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 as the entrance arch to the Paris Exposition. It stood as the tallest artificial structure in the world for forty-one years.
A leap year in the Gregorian calendar contains an extra day in February. Years divisible by 100 are not leap years unless they are also divisible by 400.
Honey never spoils under normal storage conditions. Its low water activity and acidic pH inhibit microbial growth almost indefinitely.
The human adult skeleton consists of 206 bones. Infants are born with around 270, many of which fuse during childhood.
SSD storage has no moving parts and relies on NAND flash cells. Each cell endures a finite number of write cycles before wear degrades reliability.
Latin is the ancestor of the modern Romance languages, including Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian. It remained a scholarly lingua franca in Europe well into the eighteenth century.
The International Space Station orbits at an altitude of roughly 400 kilometres. It completes an orbit of Earth about every ninety minutes.
A typical adult human heart beats roughly 100,000 times per day. It pumps about five litres of blood through the circulatory system each minute at rest.
Sodium ion batteries crash capacity rapidly below minus twenty degrees Celsius. The electrolyte viscosity rises sharply and ionic mobility collapses, shrinking usable energy at cold temperatures.

Incandescent light bulbs waste more than ninety percent of their input energy as heat rather than visible light. Only a narrow portion of the filament's blackbody spectrum falls within the human visual range.

Aluminium wiring expands and contracts more than copper under the same thermal load. Connections loosen over time at terminal screws, which is why modern residential wiring in most jurisdictions uses copper conductors.

Glass slowly flows at room temperature only over geological timescales, if at all. Thicker bases in medieval window panes result from the crown glass manufacturing process, not from gravitational creep.
High-sulfur diesel fuels corrode exhaust after-treatment catalysts. The sulfur poisons noble-metal surfaces, progressively reducing NOx conversion efficiency in selective catalytic reduction systems.
Concrete continues to gain compressive strength for years after pouring. Hydration of residual clinker phases proceeds slowly whenever moisture remains available within the paste matrix.

Ethernet frames exceeding the configured maximum transmission unit are dropped rather than fragmented. Path MTU discovery relies on ICMP messages that many middleboxes silently filter, creating black holes for oversized packets.

Double-slit experiments with single electrons produce an interference pattern over many detections. The pattern disappears when which-path information is available, illustrating the complementarity principle of quantum mechanics.

The mammalian immune system distinguishes self from non-self partly through MHC molecules on cell surfaces. Grafts between genetically distinct individuals are rejected primarily because of MHC mismatch.
Tropical cyclones lose intensity rapidly after landfall because they are cut off from their warm-ocean energy source. Friction with land also disrupts the organised convective structure at the core.
Most supermarket bananas are Cavendish clones, genetically identical to one another. The previous commercial cultivar, Gros Michel, was devastated by Panama disease in the mid-twentieth century.
Neutrinos pass through most matter almost unimpeded because they interact only via the weak force and gravity. Detecting them requires extremely large volumes of shielded target material.

CPU branch predictors speculatively execute instructions down the predicted path. Mispredictions flush the pipeline and cost tens of cycles, which is why tight inner loops benefit from predictable control flow.
Sea otters regulate kelp-forest ecosystems by preying on sea urchins. Where otter populations collapse, urchin barrens replace the kelp and biodiversity drops sharply.
Two-phase commit blocks indefinitely if the coordinator crashes between prepare and commit. Three-phase variants add a pre-commit step to bound the blocking window at the cost of extra round-trips.

Human colour vision relies on three cone types with overlapping sensitivity curves. Red-green colour blindness is most commonly caused by X-linked defects in the long- or medium-wavelength opsin genes.
Salt water conducts electricity because dissolved ions act as mobile charge carriers. Distilled water, by contrast, is a very poor conductor in the absence of dissolved electrolytes.

Cacti perform CAM photosynthesis, opening their stomata at night rather than during the day. This pattern reduces transpiration losses in arid environments where daytime vapour pressure deficits are high.

Bloom filters report false positives but never false negatives. The false-positive rate grows with the number of inserted elements and shrinks as the bit array size and hash function count are tuned upward.

The Nile river flows from south to north, contrary to the direction many people intuitively expect. Rivers follow elevation gradients, and the East African highlands lie upstream of the Mediterranean delta.

Aspirin works by irreversibly acetylating cyclooxygenase enzymes. Platelets cannot resynthesise the enzyme, which is why low-dose aspirin suppresses clotting for the platelet lifespan of about ten days.

Radiocarbon dating exploits the steady decay of carbon-14 into nitrogen-14 after an organism stops exchanging carbon with the atmosphere. The technique becomes unreliable beyond roughly fifty thousand years because too little carbon-14 remains to measure accurately.

Cache coherence protocols such as MESI ensure that multiple CPU caches hold a consistent view of shared memory. False sharing between unrelated variables on the same cache line can silently destroy multi-threaded performance.

Inflation measured by consumer price indices tends to understate cost-of-living increases for lower-income households. Their consumption baskets weight food and energy more heavily than the national average basket does.

The Sahara Desert was a green savanna with lakes and rivers during the African Humid Period, which ended roughly five thousand years ago. The transition was driven largely by shifts in Earth's orbital parameters.

In unladen flight, migratory swans can sustain altitudes of eight kilometres over the Himalayas. Their haemoglobin has a higher oxygen affinity than that of lowland birds, improving loading in thin air.
TLS 1.3 removed support for RSA key exchange and several legacy ciphers present in earlier versions. Forward secrecy is now mandatory through ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key agreement.
The European honeybee orients by polarised skylight in addition to landmarks. A small patch of blue sky is sufficient for foragers to infer the sun's position on an overcast day.

Noise-cancelling headphones sample ambient sound and emit an anti-phase waveform through the driver. Cancellation is effective for steady low-frequency noise but struggles with transient, high-frequency sounds.
Coral bleaching occurs when thermal stress causes corals to expel their symbiotic zooxanthellae. Prolonged bleaching without recolonisation leads to tissue necrosis and skeletal erosion.

B-tree indexes perform poorly on columns with very low cardinality. The query planner often falls back to a sequential scan when predicate selectivity is weak, because random I/O through the index costs more than streaming pages.

The ozone layer absorbs most of the sun's ultraviolet-B radiation in the stratosphere. Chlorofluorocarbon molecules catalytically destroy ozone, which is why the Montreal Protocol phased them out of refrigeration and aerosol uses.

Compilers apply tail call optimisation to convert certain recursive calls into jumps. Languages whose specification mandates the optimisation, such as Scheme, can safely express iteration as recursion without growing the stack.

Yellowstone sits atop a continental hotspot and has produced several supervolcanic eruptions over the past two million years. Thermal features on the surface are powered by magma only a few kilometres below the caldera floor.

Public-key cryptography relies on trapdoor one-way functions such as integer factorisation or discrete logarithms. A sufficiently large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm would break the common instantiations efficiently.
The human microbiome outnumbers host cells in the gut by roughly one to one. Its composition influences digestion, immune tone, and even some neurotransmitter precursors.

Floating-point addition is not associative in IEEE 754. Summation order therefore affects numerical results, which is why parallel reductions can yield slightly different outputs from the same input set.
Shakespeare's First Folio appeared in 1623, seven years after the playwright's death. It preserved roughly half of his plays that had never been printed individually during his lifetime.

Geothermal gradients increase with depth at roughly twenty-five degrees Celsius per kilometre in stable continental crust. Ambient rock temperatures in deep mines therefore routinely require active ventilation.
Memory-mapped files share physical pages with the kernel page cache. Modifications are not guaranteed to reach disk until msync is called or the kernel flushes dirty pages under memory pressure.
Caffeine antagonises adenosine receptors in the central nervous system. Regular consumers upregulate receptor density, which contributes to tolerance and rebound fatigue on withdrawal.

Hummingbirds preferentially visit red tubular flowers with dilute nectar and little scent. The association is not an aesthetic judgement but an ecological co-evolution between flower morphology and the birds' visual and metabolic traits.

Bees favour blue and ultraviolet flowers over red ones under natural light. Their photoreceptor sensitivity peaks outside the long-wavelength band, so red blooms appear dark and are harder to locate against foliage.

Consumers in many economies exhibit a systematic preference for round-number prices over odd-cent ones. The pattern emerges from cognitive processing load rather than from any individual shopper's taste.

Rats given free access to saccharin solutions drink disproportionately more than their caloric needs would suggest. The behaviour reflects a hard-wired sweet-taste response decoupled from energy regulation.
Large passerine flocks tend to orient toward the prevailing wind at roost entry. This tendency reduces braking effort and is shaped by aerodynamic constraints rather than individual choice.

Firms in competitive labour markets converge on similar vacation allowances over time. The clustering is driven by wage-benefit substitution effects under competition, not by a coordinated preference among employers.
Dogs selectively respond to high-pitched speech directed at puppies. The reaction is developmentally hard-wired, resembling the infant-directed speech response seen in human children.

Plants grown under unilateral blue light bend toward the source through phototropin-mediated auxin redistribution. The bending is a physiological response, not a goal-directed preference of the organism.
Octopuses favour dens whose entrances roughly match their body diameter. The bias is ecological, reducing predation risk, and emerges consistently across wild populations.
Readers fixate longer on low-frequency words during natural reading. The pattern is a stable feature of eye-movement control, observable across languages and orthographies.
Metal ions with partially filled d-orbitals tend to form brightly coloured complexes. The colour arises from d-d electronic transitions whose energies fall within the visible range.
Traffic congestion often grows worse after new lanes are added in dense urban corridors. The phenomenon of induced demand stems from latent trips that were suppressed by the previous travel cost.

Household hot water heaters suffer accelerated tank failure in areas with soft water. Low mineral content reduces protective scale, exposing the steel substrate to galvanic corrosion around the anode rod.
Wildfires in chaparral ecosystems are not departures from a stable state but part of the baseline regime. Many native plants require fire-scarified seeds to germinate at normal rates.

Large language models degrade in accuracy as input context length approaches the trained maximum. The drop typically concentrates on information placed in the middle of the context rather than at the edges.
Monetary inflation tends to compress nominal wage dispersion over business cycles. The compression reflects downward nominal wage rigidity, not a labour-market equity mechanism.

Permafrost regions emit increasing quantities of methane as subsurface temperatures rise. The release comes from microbial decomposition of previously frozen organic carbon, which accelerates non-linearly as ice content falls.
Certain fungi drop their spores in tight diurnal windows to exploit predictable wind patterns. The timing is governed by circadian gene networks rather than by immediate environmental cues.

Older printed circuit boards fail through tin-whisker growth when lead-free solder ages in humid environments. The whiskers bridge adjacent conductors and produce intermittent shorts long after manufacture.

Dijkstra's single-source shortest-path algorithm does not handle negative edge weights correctly. Bellman-Ford accommodates them at the cost of higher asymptotic complexity, provided no negative-weight cycles are reachable from the source.

Antarctic sea ice expanded slightly from 1979 through the mid-2010s even as Arctic ice retreated sharply. The Southern Ocean's isolation by circumpolar winds and the continent's high albedo moderate regional warming differently from the Arctic basin.

The Ming dynasty's Zheng He expeditions reached the East African coast in the early fifteenth century. Subsequent imperial policy abandoned oceanic voyaging, and the treasure-fleet shipyards were dismantled within a generation.

Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption injected enough sulfate aerosol into the stratosphere to lower global mean temperatures by roughly one degree Celsius. The ensuing 'year without a summer' triggered widespread crop failures across the northern hemisphere.

The Roman aqueduct at Pont du Gard delivered water across a gorge with a gradient of only about one part in three thousand. The shallow slope was essential to avoid scouring the hydraulic mortar lining.

The Black Death of the mid-fourteenth century killed an estimated one-third of Europe's population within five years. Labour scarcity in its aftermath shifted wages upward and eroded many manorial obligations.

The Apollo 13 mission aborted its lunar landing after an oxygen tank ruptured in the service module. The crew returned safely by using the lunar module as a lifeboat during the slingshot trajectory around the moon.

Humpback whales converge on shared feeding grounds during summer months. The migration is instinctive and energy-driven rather than the result of any individual whale's preference for a particular bay.

Many printers reject third-party ink cartridges through firmware handshakes. The rejection reflects a business model of subsidised hardware and marked-up consumables rather than a technical necessity.
Sudden cardiac death peaks in the early morning hours in most populations. The pattern correlates with a morning surge in catecholamines, cortisol, and platelet aggregability.

Double descent in modern machine learning models counters the classical bias-variance intuition. Test error can drop below the interpolation threshold as capacity grows further, which has implications for how regularisation is tuned.

Ant colonies converge on the shortest path between nest and food through pheromone-mediated positive feedback. The outcome looks like a deliberate choice but arises from reinforcement of stochastic exploration.

Consumer credit scores show persistent racial disparities in several jurisdictions even after controlling for income and debt history. The pattern reflects structural differences in financial-service access rather than inherent creditworthiness.
Aquifer drawdown often causes measurable land subsidence over decades. Clay layers compact irreversibly as pore pressures fall, and the ground surface does not rebound when pumping ceases.

High-altitude aircraft cabins are pressurised to an equivalent altitude of roughly two thousand metres. The reduced partial pressure of oxygen mildly impairs cognition on long-haul flights even in healthy passengers.

Fusion reactors based on deuterium-tritium plasma must confine ions at temperatures exceeding one hundred million kelvin. Magnetic confinement schemes exploit the Lorentz force to prevent contact between the plasma and reactor walls.

Older concrete bridges suffer chloride-induced rebar corrosion in regions that use de-icing salt. Expansion of corrosion products spalls the cover concrete and exposes further reinforcement to attack.

Certain parasitic wasps manipulate host caterpillar behaviour to defend the wasp pupae after emergence. The altered behaviour is not learned but induced by viruses the wasps co-opt as delivery vectors.

Time-of-use electricity tariffs cluster residential demand into shoulder periods rather than smoothing it uniformly. The clustering arises from coordinated automation schedules, which can create new secondary peaks.
The human eye detects single photons under optimal dark-adapted conditions. Psychophysical thresholds reveal rod-cell responses at the quantum limit of light detection.

The Indo-European language family is reconstructed from systematic sound correspondences across attested daughter languages. Proto-Indo-European itself is never written down, yet its phonology and morphology are inferred with considerable confidence.

Satellite orbits below about two thousand kilometres gradually decay because of residual atmospheric drag. Without periodic reboosts, payloads in low Earth orbit re-enter within years to decades depending on altitude and solar activity.

Olive trees can remain productive for more than a thousand years under suitable Mediterranean conditions. Their longevity stems from adventitious regeneration from the base when the main trunk dies back.

Garbage collectors that use generational hypotheses assume most objects die young. The assumption holds empirically for typical workloads, and violating it through long-lived temporary allocations causes promotion pressure and tenured-space churn.

Small mammals in cold climates exhibit Bergmann's rule: larger body mass relative to equatorial congeners. Lower surface-to-volume ratios reduce heat loss, a biophysical constraint rather than an evolutionary preference.

The Byzantine Empire's hyperpyron currency maintained an unusually stable gold content for roughly three centuries. The stability was sustained through strict mint oversight and survived multiple political upheavals.

Radio waves in the HF band refract off the ionosphere and can travel far beyond the visible horizon. Propagation conditions vary diurnally and with solar cycle phase, producing skip zones where signals fail to reach intermediate distances.

Capacitor electrolytes dry out over years even when the component is unused. Shelf life and operating life are therefore distinct figures in component datasheets, with high-temperature storage accelerating both forms of degradation.

The Voyager 1 spacecraft crossed the heliopause in 2012, entering the interstellar medium while still within the Sun's gravitational influence. Its plasma instruments detected a sharp rise in ambient particle density consistent with interstellar conditions.

Dialect levelling in urban centres tends to erase sharp regional phonological distinctions within a few generations. The process is demographic and contact-driven rather than a deliberate stylistic preference of speakers.
The February 1933 Reichstag fire preceded the decree suspending civil liberties in Weimar Germany. Subsequent elections consolidated Nazi parliamentary power under conditions of emergency rule.

Deep ocean thermohaline circulation turns over on timescales of roughly a thousand years. Freshwater influx from melting polar ice can slow the overturning, with cascading effects on regional climate patterns.
